belief: If I had enough faith, God would have healed me.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if you had enough faith God would have healed you, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that God always heals when faith is strong enough. Being told your illness continues because you doubt. Seeing others healed and wondering what is wrong with you. Praying hard for healing that has not come. Well-meaning people who said, “Just believe and you’ll be well.”
teaches: God can heal, and we are free to ask Him. But Scripture does not teach that every illness lasts because of weak faith. Paul, a man of great faith, pleaded three times for his thorn to be removed, and God answered, “My grace is sufficient for you.” Paul left his co-worker Trophimus sick in Miletus. God works all things together for good for those who love Him, sometimes by healing and sometimes by giving strength in weakness.
self_statements: My illness is my fault for not believing enough.
God would heal me if my faith were stronger.
Other people have more faith than I do.
I must be doing something wrong spiritually.
If I admit I’m sick, I’m confessing doubt.
God is disappointed in my weak faith.
errors: Blaming your faith for an illness with many causes.
Turning “God sometimes heals in answer to faith” into “God always heals when faith is enough.”
Measuring your faith by other people’s healing stories.
Ignoring faithful people in Scripture who were not healed.
questions: Did Paul lack faith when his thorn was not removed?
Why did Paul leave Trophimus sick?
What did God say to Paul instead of healing him?
Is my illness a measure of my faith, or part of living in a broken world?
Can God be glorified through my weakness?
Who taught me that faith always brings healing?
What does it look like to trust God while I am still sick?
truth: My illness is not proof that my faith is too weak. God can heal, and I can ask Him to. But even faithful people like Paul were not always healed. God’s grace is sufficient for me, and His power is made perfect in my weakness. I can trust Him whether He heals me now, later, or in eternity.
hw_questions: Did Paul lack faith when he wasn’t healed?
What did God say instead of healing Paul?
Is my illness a measure of my faith?
Can God be glorified in my weakness?
What does trusting God while sick look like?
hw_truths: My illness is not a measure of my faith.
God’s grace is sufficient for me.
God’s power is perfected in my weakness.
God works all things together for my good.
I can ask for healing and trust God with the answer.
God is the strength of my heart.
log: Each day, write one way God gave me strength or grace in my weakness.
name_example: But He said to Sarah, ‘My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.’
actions: and write what Paul learned through his unanswered prayer.
and also pray, “Give me Your grace for today.”
as part of trusting God, not as a lack of faith.
Talk with someone who has lived faithfully with illness
and ask how they experience God’s grace.
tracker: One way God gave me strength
prayer: Father, thank You that You can heal, and that Your grace is sufficient for me. Help me reject the lie that my illness continues because my faith is too weak. Give me strength in my weakness, peace in my waiting, and trust that You are working all things for my good. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
